title: Hydrogen Extraction for Recovery of Phenolic Compounds from Tea Wastes
author: Elnasankasim, Muhammed Allam
materials: The chemicals (DPPH, ABTS, Trolox, ascorbic acid, quercetin, 3,4,5 trihydroxybenzoic acid, potassium persulfate, Folin–Ciocalteu reagent were purchased from Merck (Darmstadt, Germany) and Sigma (MO, USA).

The extraction procedure was performed according to the method described by Alwazeer and co-workers (Alwazeer et al. 2023d). Briefly, 1 g tea waste powder was mixed with 20 mL of solvent [(pure water prepared by Millipore Milli-Q® Direct 8 Water Purification System, USA), hydrogen-rich water (HRW), magnesium water (Mg water), ethanol/Mg water (50/50, % vol), and ethanol/pure water (50/50, % vol)], followed by a 24-hr incubation at 35 °C. The evaporation of solvents was then performed.

steps.title: Gather required chemicals
steps.instruction: Obtain DPPH, ABTS, Trolox, ascorbic acid, quercetin, 3,4,5‑trihydroxybenzoic acid, potassium persulfate, and Folin–Ciocalteu reagent from Merck (Darmstadt, Germany) and Sigma (MO, USA).

steps.title: Prepare black tea waste
steps.instruction: Boil 25 g dry black tea leaves in 1 L water for 5 min, separate the leaves, dry the waste at 35 °C, mill to a fine powder, and store the powder at –80 °C.

steps.title: Extract phenolics from tea waste
steps.instruction: Mix 1 g tea‑waste powder with 20 mL of the selected solvent (pure Millipore water, hydrogen‑rich water, magnesium water, 50/50 v/v ethanol/Mg water, or 50/50 v/v ethanol/pure water), incubate for 24 h at 35 °C, then evaporate the solvent.

steps.title: Determine total phenolic content
steps.instruction: Measure the total phenolic content (TPC) of each extract using the method described by Alwazeer et al. 2023d.

steps.title: Determine total flavonoid content
steps.instruction: Measure the total flavonoid content (TFC) of each extract using the method described by Alwazeer et al. 2023d.

steps.title: Assess DPPH antioxidant activity
steps.instruction: Determine the DPPH scavenging activity of each extract according to Alwazeer et al. 2023d.

steps.title: Assess ABTS antioxidant activity
steps.instruction: Determine the ABTS scavenging activity of each extract according to Alwazeer et al. 2023d.

steps.title: Run HPLC phenolic profiling
steps.instruction: Filter each tea extract through a 0.45 µm membrane, inject 20 µL into an Agilent 1260 Infinity HPLC‑DAD equipped with an ACE Generix C18 column (250 × 4.6 mm, 5 µm), set flow to 0.8 mL/min, and apply a gradient of mobile phase A (1 % v/v orthophosphoric acid in water) and B (acetonitrile) starting at 83 % A, changing to 60 % A at 30 min and back to 83 % A at 35 min (total run 40 min); detect phenolic compounds at 350 nm and 200 nm.

steps.title: Perform statistical analysis
steps.instruction: Analyze the data by one‑way ANOVA using GraphPad Prism 9; apply Tukey’s post‑hoc test and Duncan’s multiple comparison test in IBM SPSS Statistics 26; consider differences significant at p < 0.05; the whole experiment was duplicated and each measurement performed in triplicate (n = 3).
